blurb: Hungarian herding dog with a long corded coat that looks like dreadlocks
description: The Puli is a small-to-medium Hungarian herding dog with a long, corded coat, usually black, described as intelligent, active, loyal and wary of strangers.
answer: The Puli is a small-to-medium Hungarian herding dog known for its long, corded coat, whose tight curls resemble dreadlocks. It has herded sheep on the Hungarian plain for centuries. It stands about 36 to 45 cm and is commonly described as intelligent, energetic and devoted.

body: The Magyars probably brought the Puli to Hungary in the 9th century, and it has worked as a sheepdog on the Hungarian plain ever since. It often worked alongside the much larger Komondor: the Puli herded and guarded the flock by day, the Komondor guarded it at night. Shepherds reportedly paid as much as a year's salary for a good Puli. As intensive farming replaced extensive shepherding in the early 20th century, the breed became more of a house dog. In 1935 the US Department of Agriculture imported four Pulis for herding experiments.

The Puli is a solid-coloured dog, usually black, less often white, grey or cream; white Pulis are not albino and have dark pigment. The standard gives about 42 cm for females and 43 cm for males. The corded coat results from a controlled matting process, can grow to the ground with age, and may be trimmed short. The breed has little to no shedding.

The Puli is commonly described as intelligent, sensitive, fun-loving and courageous, but at times tough and headstrong. It is said to be loyal and close to its owners, very friendly towards children, wary of strangers and protective of its territory. It keeps a playful, puppy-like manner throughout life.

Sources describe it as highly active, needing plenty of exercise and space, ideally a house with a garden; kept confined it may grow restless, hyperactive or aloof. Early obedience training and socialization are recommended. The corded coat needs considerable grooming to stay clean. Pulis compete in agility, obedience, flyball, tracking and herding.
The source text names no specific health conditions. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.a: The breed has little to no shedding, but its corded coat needs considerable grooming.

faq.q: How big does a Puli get?
faq.a: It stands about 36 to 45 cm and weighs roughly 10 to 15 kg.
The breed is commonly described as very friendly, especially towards children, though sensitive and wary of strangers.

faq.q: Is the Puli recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 55 in Group 1, Sheepdogs and Cattle Dogs.
